- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.17) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.22) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Forecast tends to lag the true price by 1–3 days in downward moves — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per day for negative sentiment.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged peak — reduce forecast by 2–4% for 2–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high sentiment + high price, model overestimates — apply downward correction of 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment is trending upward but price is declining.
